source_file: 1 1 fractions as percentages you might have heard statements like   mega sale   up to 50  off   or  hiya scored 83  in her board exams   do you know what the symbol     means  this symbol is read as per cent  the word  per cent  is derived from the latin phrase  per centum   meaning  by the hundred  or  out of hundred   so  25 per cent  25   means 25 out of every 100   like 25 people out of 100  25 rupees out of 100 rupees  or 25 marks out of 100 marks  if we say 50  of some quantity s  it means 50    50   1 100   s  50 times the unit fraction of s    50 100   s   1 2s  thus  percentages are simply fractions where the denominator is 100  examples  20    20 100   2 10   1 5  33    33 100  we saw that percentages are just fractions  given any fraction  can we express it as a percentage  yes  let us see how  expressing fractions as percentages example 1  surya wants to use a deep orange colour to capture the sunset  he mixes some red paint and yellow paint to make this colour  the red paint makes up 3 4 of this mixture  what percentage of the colour is made with red  3 4 is 3 out of every 4  that is  6 out of every 8  equivalent fraction   that is  30 out of every 40  that is  75 out of every 100  this means 75   3 4    6 8   30 40   75 100 fractions in disguise 1  ganita prakash   grade 8   part ii 2 explaining this in a different way  to express 3 4 as a percentage  we need to find its equivalent fraction with 100 as the denominator  two ways of going ahead are shown below  me

concepts.title: Understanding Percentages
concepts.definition: A percentage is a specific way of representing a part of a whole where the total is always considered to be 100.
concepts.key_idea: A percent always measures against a whole of 100.
question_patterns: explain what the word percent tells us about a whole of 100
what does 25 percent mean
express 25 out of 100 as a percentage
calculate the percentage of a quantity given its value out of 100
What does 40 percent of a class mean?
If 35 of 100 students walk, state it as a percent.

solution_steps.action: Divide the part by the total whole
solution_steps.explain: Find the ratio of the given quantity to the total.
Convert the ratio to a per-hundred value.

solution_steps.action: recover the part from the percentage to verify
solution_steps.explain: part = percentage x whole / 100, confirming the round-trip

concepts.title: Converting Fractions to Percentages
concepts.definition: Scale any fraction so its bottom count reads 100 -- or shift it by a factor of 100 -- to state it as a percent.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying a fraction by 100 converts it to its percentage form.
question_patterns: write the paint-mix fraction 3/4 as a percentage
express the fraction 3/4 as a percentage
convert 2/5 to percentage
what percentage of the mixture is red paint if it is 3/4 of the total
Write 7/20 as a percent.
Turn 0.45 into a percentage.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the numerator by 100 and divide by the denominator.

solution_steps.action: for a decimal, multiply directly by 100
solution_steps.explain: A decimal like 0.45 becomes 45 percent by shifting the decimal point two places right

solution_steps.action: verify by converting back to a fraction
solution_steps.explain: Divide the percentage by 100 to recover the original fraction

concepts.title: Finding the Value of a Percentage
concepts.definition: Calculating the actual numerical value that represents a given percentage of a total quantity.
concepts.key_idea: The word 'of' in percentage problems indicates multiplication.
question_patterns: calculate 25 percent of 120 marks
find 25% of 120
calculate 80% of 75 marks
what is 15% of 60
how much is 40% of 50
How much is 60 percent of 400?
Calculate 5 percent of 2500.

solution_steps.action: Convert percentage to decimal or fraction
solution_steps.explain: Divide the percentage by 100.
Multiply the fraction by the whole amount to find the part.

solution_steps.action: to find the total from a known percentage value
solution_steps.explain: total = value x 100 / percent

concepts.title: Ratios to Percentages
concepts.definition: Turn each part of a ratio into its slice of the whole, stated per 100.
concepts.key_idea: Add the ratio parts first; that sum becomes the whole.
question_patterns: the ratio of millet to water is 2:7, find the percentage of millet
convert the ratio 10:80:10 into percentages
what percentage does each part of the ratio 2:3 represent
Divide 700 between two people in ratio 3:4 -- what percent gets each?
Two chemicals mix 5:3 -- percent of each in the blend?

solution_steps.explain: Add all the components of the ratio together.

solution_steps.action: Calculate percentage of the specific part
solution_steps.explain: Divide the specific part by total parts and multiply by 100.

solution_steps.action: find the actual quantity for each part
solution_steps.explain: quantity = (part_ratio / total_parts) x total_amount

concepts.title: Percentage Increase or Decrease
concepts.definition: Compare a change against the starting figure, stated per 100.
concepts.key_idea: Always use the original (initial) value as the base for calculation.
question_patterns: find the percentage increase in price from 30 to 42
calculate the percentage decrease in footfall from 160 to 100
what is the rate of inflation if price rose from 38 to 42
Price rose from 80 to 100 -- percent rise?
A crowd fell from 2000 to 1500 -- percent fall?

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the smaller value from the larger value.
Divide the change by the original value and multiply by 100.

solution_steps.action: find the new value from a percentage change
solution_steps.explain: new_value = original_value x (1 + percent_change / 100) for increase, or (1 - percent_change / 100) for decrease

concepts.title: Profit and Loss Percentage
concepts.definition: State the gain or shortfall per 100 of what you paid.
concepts.key_idea: Work the percent on the buying price, never the selling price.
question_patterns: find the profit percentage if CP is 300 and SP is 430
calculate loss percentage if rice bought at 35 is sold at 30
what is the profit margin on a geometry box bought for 75 and sold for 110
Bought at 250, sold at 300 -- percent gain?
CP 400, SP 360 -- percent shortfall?

solution_steps.explain: Subtract CP from SP for profit, or SP from CP for loss.
Divide the difference by the cost price and multiply by 100.

solution_steps.action: find the selling price from a desired profit percentage
solution_steps.explain: sp = cp x (1 + profit_percent / 100)

concepts.title: Simple Interest (No Compounding)
concepts.definition: The charge grows only on the sum first deposited, flat for the whole term.
concepts.key_idea: The principal remains constant throughout the time period.
question_patterns: find the amount after 3 years on 6000 at 10% interest without compounding
calculate simple interest on 50000 for 3 years at 7% p.a.
how much interest is earned on a deposit of p for t years at r%
Find the charge on 9000 at 6 percent for 4 years, flat.
A deposit of p at r percent for t years -- how much accumulates?

solution_steps.explain: Multiply principal, rate, and time, then divide by 100.
Add the interest to the original principal.

solution_steps.action: find the principal from the total amount
solution_steps.explain: principal = total_amount / (1 + rate x time / 100)

concepts.title: Compound Interest (Annual)
concepts.definition: Interest calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.
concepts.key_idea: Each year's charge joins the balance before the next year is worked out.
question_patterns: calculate amount for 6000 at 10% p.a. compounded annually for 3 years
find the population after 3 years if it grows at 3% annually
what is the final value of 20000 after 2 years at 10% compounded
What does 12000 become after 2 years at 8 percent, compounded yearly?
Find the compounded value of p at r percent for t years.

solution_steps.explain: Add 1 to the decimal rate of interest.
Multiply principal by the growth factor raised to the power of time.
compound interest = total amount minus principal

concepts.title: Depreciation
concepts.definition: An asset sheds value year by year, usually quoted per 100 per year.
concepts.key_idea: Depreciation is like negative compound growth.
question_patterns: a TV bought for 21000 depreciates by 5% in one year, find its value
population reduces by 10% every decade, find population after 3 decades
calculate the value of a bike after 2 years if it loses 10% value annually
A machine worth 50000 loses 10 percent yearly -- value after 2 years?
Quote the rule for yearly shrinking value.

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the decimal rate from 1.
Multiply initial value by the reduction factor raised to the power of time.
depreciation = initial value minus final value
